1:1.web: The beginning of the Good News of Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
1:1.kjv: The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;

1:2.web: As it is written in the prophets, “Behold, I send my messenger before your face, who will prepare your way before you:
1:2.kjv: As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.

1:3.web: the voice of one crying in the wilderness, ‘Make ready the way of the Lord! Make his paths straight!’”
1:3.kjv: The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.

1:4.web: John came baptizing in the wilderness and preaching the baptism of repentance for forgiveness of sins.
1:4.kjv: John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.

1:5.web: All the country of Judea and all those of Jerusalem went out to him. They were baptized by him in the Jordan river, confessing their sins.
1:5.kjv: And there went out unto him all the land of Judaea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.

1:6.web: John was clothed with camel’s hair and a leather belt around his waist. He ate locusts and wild honey.
1:6.kjv: And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;

1:7.web: He preached, saying, “After me comes he who is mightier than I, the thong of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and loosen.
1:7.kjv: And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.

1:8.web: I baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit.”
1:8.kjv: I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.

1:9.web: In those days, Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized by John in the Jordan.
1:9.kjv: And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.

1:10.web: Immediately coming up from the water, he saw the heavens parting, and the Spirit descending on him like a dove.
1:10.kjv: And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him:

1:11.web: A voice came out of the sky, “You are my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.”
1:11.kjv: And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.

1:12.web: Immediately the Spirit drove him out into the wilderness.
1:12.kjv: And immediately the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.

1:13.web: He was there in the wilderness forty days tempted by Satan. He was with the wild animals; and the angels were serving him.
1:13.kjv: And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.

1:14.web: Now after John was taken into custody, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the Good News of God’s Kingdom,
1:14.kjv: Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,

1:15.web: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and God’s Kingdom is at hand! Repent, and believe in the Good News.”
1:15.kjv: And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.

1:16.web: Passing along by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew the brother of Simon casting a net into the sea, for they were fishermen.
1:16.kjv: Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.

1:17.web: Jesus said to them, “Come after me, and I will make you into fishers for men.”
1:17.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.

1:18.web: Immediately they left their nets, and followed him.
1:18.kjv: And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.

1:19.web: Going on a little further from there, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John, his brother, who were also in the boat mending the nets.
1:19.kjv: And when he had gone a little farther thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.

1:20.web: Immediately he called them, and they left their father, Zebedee, in the boat with the hired servants, and went after him.
1:20.kjv: And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.

1:21.web: They went into Capernaum, and immediately on the Sabbath day he entered into the synagogue and taught.
1:21.kjv: And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught.

1:22.web: They were astonished at his teaching, for he taught them as having authority, and not as the scribes.
1:22.kjv: And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.

1:23.web: Immediately there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried out,
1:23.kjv: And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,

1:24.web: saying, “Ha! What do we have to do with you, Jesus, you Nazarene? Have you come to destroy us? I know you who you are: the Holy One of God!”
1:24.kjv: Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.

1:25.web: Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet, and come out of him!”
1:25.kjv: And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.

1:26.web: The unclean spirit, convulsing him and crying with a loud voice, came out of him.
1:26.kjv: And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him.

1:27.web: They were all amazed, so that they questioned among themselves, saying, “What is this? A new teaching? For with authority he commands even the unclean spirits, and they obey him!”
1:27.kjv: And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him.

1:28.web: The report of him went out immediately everywhere into all the region of Galilee and its surrounding area.
1:28.kjv: And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee.

bsb: Jesus and His companions had left
1:29.web: Immediately, when they had come out of the synagogue, they came into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
1:29.kjv: And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.

1:30.web: Now Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick with a fever, and immediately they told him about her.
1:30.kjv: But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her.

1:31.web: He came and took her by the hand, and raised her up. The fever left her, and she served them.
1:31.kjv: And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.

1:32.web: At evening, when the sun had set, they brought to him all who were sick, and those who were possessed by demons.
1:32.kjv: And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils.

1:33.web: All the city was gathered together at the door.
1:33.kjv: And all the city was gathered together at the door.

1:34.web: He healed many who were sick with various diseases, and cast out many demons. He didn’t allow the demons to speak, because they knew him.
1:34.kjv: And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases, and cast out many devils; and suffered not the devils to speak, because they knew him.

1:35.web: Early in the morning, while it was still dark, he rose up and went out, and departed into a deserted place, and prayed there.
1:35.kjv: And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.

1:36.web: Simon and those who were with him followed after him;
1:36.kjv: And Simon and they that were with him followed after him.

1:37.web: and they found him, and told him, “Everyone is looking for you.”
1:37.kjv: And when they had found him, they said unto him, All men seek for thee.

1:38.web: He said to them, “Let’s go elsewhere into the next towns, that I may preach there also, because I came out for this reason.”
1:38.kjv: And he said unto them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.

1:39.web: He went into their synagogues throughout all Galilee, preaching and casting out demons.
1:39.kjv: And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out devils.

1:40.web: A leper came to him, begging him, kneeling down to him, and saying to him, “If you want to, you can make me clean.”
1:40.kjv: And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.

1:41.web: Being moved with compassion, he stretched out his hand, and touched him, and said to him, “I want to. Be made clean.”
1:41.kjv: And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.

1:42.web: When he had said this, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was made clean.
1:42.kjv: And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.

1:43.web: He strictly warned him, and immediately sent him out,
1:43.kjv: And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;

1:44.web: and said to him, “See you say nothing to anybody, but go show yourself to the priest, and offer for your cleansing the things which Moses commanded, for a testimony to them.”
1:44.kjv: And saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

1:45.web: But he went out, and began to proclaim it much, and to spread about the matter, so that Jesus could no more openly enter into a city, but was outside in desert places: and they came to him from everywhere.
1:45.kjv: But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.

2:1.web: When he entered again into Capernaum after some days, it was heard that he was in the house.
2:1.kjv: And again he entered into Capernaum, after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house.

2:2.web: Immediately many were gathered together, so that there was no more room, not even around the door; and he spoke the word to them.
2:2.kjv: And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.

2:3.web: Four people came, carrying a paralytic to him.
2:3.kjv: And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.

2:4.web: When they could not come near to him for the crowd, they removed the roof where he was. When they had broken it up, they let down the mat that the paralytic was lying on.
2:4.kjv: And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.

2:5.web: Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, “Son, your sins are forgiven you.”
2:5.kjv: When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.

2:6.web: But there were some of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
2:6.kjv: But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,

2:7.web: “Why does this man speak blasphemies like that? Who can forgive sins but God alone?”
2:7.kjv: Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?

2:8.web: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, said to them, “Why do you reason these things in your hearts?
2:8.kjv: And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?

2:9.web: Which is easier, to tell the paralytic, ‘Your sins are forgiven;’ or to say, ‘Arise, and take up your bed, and walk?’
2:9.kjv: Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?

2:10.web: But that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralytic—
2:10.kjv: But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)

2:11.web: “I tell you, arise, take up your mat, and go to your house.”
2:11.kjv: I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

2:12.web: He arose, and immediately took up the mat, and went out in front of them all; so that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, “We never saw anything like this!”
2:12.kjv: And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.

2:13.web: He went out again by the seaside. All the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
2:13.kjv: And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.

2:14.web: As he passed by, he saw Levi, the son of Alphaeus, sitting at the tax office, and he said to him, “Follow me.” And he arose and followed him.
2:14.kjv: And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.

2:15.web: He was reclining at the table in his house, and many tax collectors and sinners sat down with Jesus and his disciples, for there were many, and they followed him.
2:15.kjv: And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

2:16.web: The scribes and the Pharisees, when they saw that he was eating with the sinners and tax collectors, said to his disciples, “Why is it that he eats and drinks with tax collectors and sinners?”
2:16.kjv: And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?

2:17.web: When Jesus heard it, he said to them, “Those who are healthy have no need for a physician, but those who are sick. I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
2:17.kjv: When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

2:18.web: John’s disciples and the Pharisees were fasting, and they came and asked him, “Why do John’s disciples and the disciples of the Pharisees fast, but your disciples don’t fast?”
2:18.kjv: And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

2:19.web: Jesus said to them, “Can the groomsmen fast while the bridegroom is with them? As long as they have the bridegroom with them, they can’t fast.
2:19.kjv: And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.

2:20.web: But the days will come when the bridegroom will be taken away from them, and then will they fast in that day.
2:20.kjv: But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.

2:21.web: No one sews a piece of unshrunk cloth on an old garment, or else the patch shrinks and the new tears away from the old, and a worse hole is made.
2:21.kjv: No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.

2:22.web: No one puts new wine into old wineskins, or else the new wine will burst the skins, and the wine pours out, and the skins will be destroyed; but they put new wine into fresh wineskins.”
2:22.kjv: And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.

2:23.web: He was going on the Sabbath day through the grain fields, and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of grain.
2:23.kjv: And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.

2:24.web: The Pharisees said to him, “Behold, why do they do that which is not lawful on the Sabbath day?”
2:24.kjv: And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?

2:25.web: He said to them, “Did you never read what David did, when he had need, and was hungry—he, and those who were with him?
2:25.kjv: And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?

2:26.web: How he entered into God’s house at the time of Abiathar the high priest, and ate the show bread, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests, and gave also to those who were with him?”
2:26.kjv: How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?

2:27.web: He said to them, “The Sabbath was made for man, not man for the Sabbath.
2:27.kjv: And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:

2:28.web: Therefore the Son of Man is lord even of the Sabbath.”
2:28.kjv: Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

3:1.web: He entered again into the synagogue, and there was a man there who had his hand withered.
3:1.kjv: And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand.

3:2.web: They watched him, whether he would heal him on the Sabbath day, that they might accuse him.
3:2.kjv: And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.

3:3.web: He said to the man who had his hand withered, “Stand up.”
3:3.kjv: And he saith unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.

3:4.web: He said to them, “Is it lawful on the Sabbath day to do good, or to do harm? To save a life, or to kill?” But they were silent.
3:4.kjv: And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.

3:5.web: When he had looked around at them with anger, being grieved at the hardening of their hearts, he said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was restored as healthy as the other.
3:5.kjv: And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

3:6.web: The Pharisees went out, and immediately conspired with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
3:6.kjv: And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.

3:7.web: Jesus withdrew to the sea with his disciples, and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, from Judea,
3:7.kjv: But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,

3:8.web: from Jerusalem, from Idumaea, beyond the Jordan, and those from around Tyre and Sidon. A great multitude, hearing what great things he did, came to him.
3:8.kjv: And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.

3:9.web: He spoke to his disciples that a little boat should stay near him because of the crowd, so that they wouldn’t press on him.
3:9.kjv: And he spake to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.

3:10.web: For he had healed many, so that as many as had diseases pressed on him that they might touch him.
3:10.kjv: For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.

3:11.web: The unclean spirits, whenever they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, “You are the Son of God!”
3:11.kjv: And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.

3:12.web: He sternly warned them that they should not make him known.
3:12.kjv: And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.

3:13.web: He went up into the mountain, and called to himself those whom he wanted, and they went to him.
3:13.kjv: And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.

3:14.web: He appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them out to preach,
3:14.kjv: And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,

3:15.web: and to have authority to heal sicknesses and to cast out demons:
3:15.kjv: And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:

3:16.web: Simon (to whom he gave the name Peter);

3:17.web: James the son of Zebedee; and John, the brother of James, (whom he called Boanerges, which means, Sons of Thunder);
3:17.kjv: And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:

3:18.web: Andrew; Philip; Bartholomew; Matthew; Thomas; James, the son of Alphaeus; Thaddaeus; Simon the Zealot;
3:18.kjv: And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,

3:19.web: and Judas Iscariot, who also betrayed him. Then he came into a house.
3:19.kjv: And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.

3:20.web: The multitude came together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
3:20.kjv: And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.

bsb: He is out of His mind.”
3:21.web: When his friends heard it, they went out to seize him: for they said, “He is insane.”
3:21.kjv: And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.

3:22.web: The scribes who came down from Jerusalem said, “He has Beelzebul,” and, “By the prince of the demons he casts out the demons.”
3:22.kjv: And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.

3:23.web: He summoned them, and said to them in parables, “How can Satan cast out Satan?
3:23.kjv: And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?

3:24.web: If a kingdom is divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
3:24.kjv: And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.

3:25.web: If a house is divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
3:25.kjv: And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.

3:26.web: If Satan has risen up against himself, and is divided, he can’t stand, but has an end.
3:26.kjv: And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.

3:27.web: But no one can enter into the house of the strong man to plunder, unless he first binds the strong man; and then he will plunder his house.
3:27.kjv: No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.

3:28.web: Most certainly I tell you, all sins of the descendants of man will be forgiven, including their blasphemies with which they may blaspheme;
3:28.kjv: Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:

3:29.web: but whoever may blaspheme against the Holy Spirit never has forgiveness, but is subject to eternal condemnation.”
3:29.kjv: But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:

3:30.web: —because they said, “He has an unclean spirit.”
3:30.kjv: Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.

3:31.web: His mother and his brothers came, and standing outside, they sent to him, calling him.
3:31.kjv: There came then his brethren and his mother, and, standing without, sent unto him, calling him.

3:32.web: A multitude was sitting around him, and they told him, “Behold, your mother, your brothers, and your sisters are outside looking for you.”
3:32.kjv: And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.

3:33.web: He answered them, “Who are my mother and my brothers?”
3:33.kjv: And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?

3:34.web: Looking around at those who sat around him, he said, “Behold, my mother and my brothers!
3:34.kjv: And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!

3:35.web: For whoever does the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.”
3:35.kjv: For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.

4:1.web: Again he began to teach by the seaside. A great multitude was gathered to him, so that he entered into a boat in the sea, and sat down. All the multitude were on the land by the sea.
4:1.kjv: And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.

4:2.web: He taught them many things in parables, and told them in his teaching,
4:2.kjv: And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine,

4:3.web: “Listen! Behold, the farmer went out to sow,
4:3.kjv: Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:

4:4.web: and as he sowed, some seed fell by the road, and the birds came and devoured it.
4:4.kjv: And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.

4:5.web: Others fell on the rocky ground, where it had little soil, and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of soil.
4:5.kjv: And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:

4:6.web: When the sun had risen, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
4:6.kjv: But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.

4:7.web: Others fell among the thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
4:7.kjv: And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.

4:8.web: Others fell into the good ground, and yielded fruit, growing up and increasing. Some produced thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times as much.”
4:8.kjv: And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.

4:9.web: He said, “Whoever has ears to hear, let him hear.”
4:9.kjv: And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.

4:10.web: When he was alone, those who were around him with the twelve asked him about the parables.
4:10.kjv: And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable.

4:11.web: He said to them, “To you is given the mystery of God’s Kingdom, but to those who are outside, all things are done in parables,
4:11.kjv: And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:

4:12.web: that ‘seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest perhaps they should turn again, and their sins should be forgiven them.’”
4:12.kjv: That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.

4:13.web: He said to them, “Don’t you understand this parable? How will you understand all of the parables?
4:13.kjv: And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?

4:15.web: The ones by the road are the ones where the word is sown; and when they have heard, immediately Satan comes, and takes away the word which has been sown in them.
4:15.kjv: And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.

4:16.web: These in the same way are those who are sown on the rocky places, who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with joy.
4:16.kjv: And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;

4:17.web: They have no root in themselves, but are short-lived. When oppression or persecution arises because of the word, immediately they stumble.
4:17.kjv: And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.

4:18.web: Others are those who are sown among the thorns. These are those who have heard the word,
4:18.kjv: And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,

4:19.web: and the cares of this age, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.
4:19.kjv: And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

4:20.web: Those which were sown on the good ground are those who hear the word, and accept it, and bear fruit, some thirty times, some sixty times, and some one hundred times.”
4:20.kjv: And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.

4:21.web: He said to them, “Is the lamp brought to be put under a basket or under a bed? Isn’t it put on a stand?
4:21.kjv: And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?

4:22.web: For there is nothing hidden, except that it should be made known; neither was anything made secret, but that it should come to light.
4:22.kjv: For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.

4:23.web: If any man has ears to hear, let him hear.”
4:23.kjv: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

bsb: you use, it will be measured
4:24.web: He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With whatever measure you measure, it will be measured to you, and more will be given to you who hear.
4:24.kjv: And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.

4:25.web: For whoever has, to him will more be given, and he who doesn’t have, even that which he has will be taken away from him.”
4:25.kjv: For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.

4:26.web: He said, “God’s Kingdom is as if a man should cast seed on the earth,
4:26.kjv: And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;

4:27.web: and should sleep and rise night and day, and the seed should spring up and grow, though he doesn’t know how.
4:27.kjv: And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.

4:28.web: For the earth bears fruit: first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear.
4:28.kjv: For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.

4:29.web: But when the fruit is ripe, immediately he puts in the sickle, because the harvest has come.”
4:29.kjv: But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.

4:30.web: He said, “How will we liken God’s Kingdom? Or with what parable will we illustrate it?
4:30.kjv: And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?

4:31.web: It’s like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, though it is less than all the seeds that are on the earth,
4:31.kjv: It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:

4:32.web: yet when it is sown, grows up, and becomes greater than all the herbs, and puts out great branches, so that the birds of the sky can lodge under its shadow.”
4:32.kjv: But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.

4:33.web: With many such parables he spoke the word to them, as they were able to hear it.
4:33.kjv: And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.

bsb: He did not tell them anything
4:34.web: Without a parable he didn’t speak to them; but privately to his own disciples he explained everything.
4:34.kjv: But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.

4:35.web: On that day, when evening had come, he said to them, “Let’s go over to the other side.”
4:35.kjv: And the same day, when the even was come, he saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side.

4:36.web: Leaving the multitude, they took him with them, even as he was, in the boat. Other small boats were also with him.
4:36.kjv: And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships.

4:37.web: A big wind storm arose, and the waves beat into the boat, so much that the boat was already filled.
4:37.kjv: And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.

4:38.web: He himself was in the stern, asleep on the cushion, and they woke him up, and told him, “Teacher, don’t you care that we are dying?”
4:38.kjv: And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?

4:39.web: He awoke, and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, “Peace! Be still!” The wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
4:39.kjv: And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.

4:40.web: He said to them, “Why are you so afraid? How is it that you have no faith?”
4:40.kjv: And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?

4:41.web: They were greatly afraid, and said to one another, “Who then is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?”
4:41.kjv: And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?

5:1.web: They came to the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
5:1.kjv: And they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.

5:2.web: When he had come out of the boat, immediately a man with an unclean spirit met him out of the tombs.
5:2.kjv: And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,

5:3.web: He lived in the tombs. Nobody could bind him any more, not even with chains,
5:3.kjv: Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:

5:4.web: because he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been torn apart by him, and the fetters broken in pieces. Nobody had the strength to tame him.
5:4.kjv: Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.

5:5.web: Always, night and day, in the tombs and in the mountains, he was crying out, and cutting himself with stones.
5:5.kjv: And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.

5:6.web: When he saw Jesus from afar, he ran and bowed down to him,
5:6.kjv: But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,

5:7.web: and crying out with a loud voice, he said, “What have I to do with you, Jesus, you Son of the Most High God? I adjure you by God, don’t torment me.”
5:7.kjv: And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.

5:8.web: For he said to him, “Come out of the man, you unclean spirit!”
5:8.kjv: For he said unto him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.

5:9.web: He asked him, “What is your name?” He said to him, “My name is Legion, for we are many.”
5:9.kjv: And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.

5:10.web: He begged him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
5:10.kjv: And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.

5:11.web: Now on the mountainside there was a great herd of pigs feeding.
5:11.kjv: Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.

5:12.web: All the demons begged him, saying, “Send us into the pigs, that we may enter into them.”
5:12.kjv: And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.

5:13.web: At once Jesus gave them permission. The unclean spirits came out and entered into the pigs. The herd of about two thousand rushed down the steep bank into the sea, and they were drowned in the sea.
5:13.kjv: And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.

5:14.web: Those who fed them fled, and told it in the city and in the country. The people came to see what it was that had happened.
5:14.kjv: And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.

5:15.web: They came to Jesus, and saw him who had been possessed by demons sitting, clothed, and in his right mind, even him who had the legion; and they were afraid.
5:15.kjv: And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.

5:16.web: Those who saw it declared to them what happened to him who was possessed by demons, and about the pigs.
5:16.kjv: And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine.

5:17.web: They began to beg him to depart from their region.
5:17.kjv: And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.

bsb: who had been possessed by the demons
5:18.web: As he was entering into the boat, he who had been possessed by demons begged him that he might be with him.
5:18.kjv: And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.

5:19.web: He didn’t allow him, but said to him, “Go to your house, to your friends, and tell them what great things the Lord has done for you, and how he had mercy on you.”
5:19.kjv: Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.

5:20.web: He went his way, and began to proclaim in Decapolis how Jesus had done great things for him, and everyone marveled.
5:20.kjv: And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.

5:21.web: When Jesus had crossed back over in the boat to the other side, a great multitude was gathered to him; and he was by the sea.
5:21.kjv: And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea.

5:22.web: Behold, one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name, came; and seeing him, he fell at his feet,
5:22.kjv: And, behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,

5:23.web: and begged him much, saying, “My little daughter is at the point of death. Please come and lay your hands on her, that she may be made healthy, and live.”
5:23.kjv: And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.

5:24.web: He went with him, and a great multitude followed him, and they pressed upon him on all sides.
5:24.kjv: And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.

5:25.web: A certain woman, who had an issue of blood for twelve years,
5:25.kjv: And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,

5:26.web: and had suffered many things by many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was no better, but rather grew worse,
5:26.kjv: And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,

5:27.web: having heard the things concerning Jesus, came up behind him in the crowd, and touched his clothes.
5:27.kjv: When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.

5:28.web: For she said, “If I just touch his clothes, I will be made well.”
5:28.kjv: For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.

5:29.web: Immediately the flow of her blood was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was healed of her affliction.
5:29.kjv: And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.

5:30.web: Immediately Jesus, perceiving in himself that the power had gone out from him, turned around in the crowd, and asked, “Who touched my clothes?”
5:30.kjv: And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?

5:31.web: His disciples said to him, “You see the multitude pressing against you, and you say, ‘Who touched me?’”
5:31.kjv: And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?

5:32.web: He looked around to see her who had done this thing.
5:32.kjv: And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.

5:33.web: But the woman, fearing and trembling, knowing what had been done to her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
5:33.kjv: But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.

5:34.web: He said to her, “Daughter, your faith has made you well. Go in peace, and be cured of your disease.”
5:34.kjv: And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.

5:35.web: While he was still speaking, people came from the synagogue ruler’s house saying, “Your daughter is dead. Why bother the Teacher any more?”
5:35.kjv: While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?

5:36.web: But Jesus, when he heard the message spoken, immediately said to the ruler of the synagogue, “Don’t be afraid, only believe.”
5:36.kjv: As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.

5:37.web: He allowed no one to follow him, except Peter, James, and John the brother of James.
5:37.kjv: And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.

5:38.web: He came to the synagogue ruler’s house, and he saw an uproar, weeping, and great wailing.
5:38.kjv: And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.

5:39.web: When he had entered in, he said to them, “Why do you make an uproar and weep? The child is not dead, but is asleep.”
5:39.kjv: And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.

5:40.web: They ridiculed him. But he, having put them all out, took the father of the child, her mother, and those who were with him, and went in where the child was lying.
5:40.kjv: And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.

5:41.web: Taking the child by the hand, he said to her, “Talitha cumi!” which means, being interpreted, “Girl, I tell you, get up!”
5:41.kjv: And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.

5:42.web: Immediately the girl rose up and walked, for she was twelve years old. They were amazed with great amazement.
5:42.kjv: And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.

5:43.web: He strictly ordered them that no one should know this, and commanded that something should be given to her to eat.
5:43.kjv: And he charged them straitly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.

6:1.web: He went out from there. He came into his own country, and his disciples followed him.
6:1.kjv: And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

6:2.web: When the Sabbath had come, he began to teach in the synagogue, and many hearing him were astonished, saying, “Where did this man get these things?” and, “What is the wisdom that is given to this man, that such mighty works come about by his hands?
6:2.kjv: And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?

6:3.web: Isn’t this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and brother of James, Joses, Judah, and Simon? Aren’t his sisters here with us?” They were offended at him.
6:3.kjv: Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.

6:4.web: Jesus said to them, “A prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, and among his own relatives, and in his own house.”
6:4.kjv: But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.

6:5.web: He could do no mighty work there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people, and healed them.
6:5.kjv: And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.

6:6.web: He marveled because of their unbelief. He went around the villages teaching.
6:6.kjv: And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.

6:7.web: He called to himself the twelve, and began to send them out two by two; and he gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
6:7.kjv: And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;

6:8.web: He commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, except a staff only: no bread, no wallet, no money in their purse,
6:8.kjv: And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:

6:9.web: but to wear sandals, and not put on two tunics.
6:9.kjv: But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.

6:10.web: He said to them, “Wherever you enter into a house, stay there until you depart from there.
6:10.kjv: And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place.

6:11.web: Whoever will not receive you nor hear you, as you depart from there, shake off the dust that is under your feet for a testimony against them. Assuredly, I tell you, it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah in the day of judgment than for that city!”
6:11.kjv: And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.

6:12.web: They went out and preached that people should repent.
6:12.kjv: And they went out, and preached that men should repent.

6:13.web: They cast out many demons, and anointed many with oil who were sick, and healed them.
6:13.kjv: And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.

6:14.web: King Herod heard this, for his name had become known, and he said, “John the Baptizer has risen from the dead, and therefore these powers are at work in him.”
6:14.kjv: And king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.

6:15.web: But others said, “He is Elijah.” Others said, “He is a prophet, or like one of the prophets.”
6:15.kjv: Others said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.

6:16.web: But Herod, when he heard this, said, “This is John, whom I beheaded. He has risen from the dead.”
6:16.kjv: But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.

6:17.web: For Herod himself had sent out and arrested John, and bound him in prison for the sake of Herodias, his brother Philip’s wife, for he had married her.
6:17.kjv: For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: for he had married her.

6:18.web: For John said to Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother’s wife.”
6:18.kjv: For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.

6:19.web: Herodias set herself against him, and desired to kill him, but she couldn’t,
6:19.kjv: Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:

6:20.web: for Herod feared John, knowing that he was a righteous and holy man, and kept him safe. When he heard him, he did many things, and he heard him gladly.
6:20.kjv: For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.

6:21.web: Then a convenient day came, that Herod on his birthday made a supper for his nobles, the high officers, and the chief men of Galilee.
6:21.kjv: And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;

6:22.web: When the daughter of Herodias herself came in and danced, she pleased Herod and those sitting with him. The king said to the young lady, “Ask me whatever you want, and I will give it to you.”
6:22.kjv: And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.

6:23.web: He swore to her, “Whatever you shall ask of me, I will give you, up to half of my kingdom.”
6:23.kjv: And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.

6:24.web: She went out, and said to her mother, “What shall I ask?” She said, “The head of John the Baptizer.”
6:24.kjv: And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.

6:25.web: She came in immediately with haste to the king, and asked, “I want you to give me right now the head of John the Baptizer on a platter.”
6:25.kjv: And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.

6:26.web: The king was exceedingly sorry, but for the sake of his oaths, and of his dinner guests, he didn’t wish to refuse her.
6:26.kjv: And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.

6:27.web: Immediately the king sent out a soldier of his guard, and commanded to bring John’s head, and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
6:27.kjv: And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,

6:28.web: and brought his head on a platter, and gave it to the young lady; and the young lady gave it to her mother.
6:28.kjv: And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.

6:29.web: When his disciples heard this, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
6:29.kjv: And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.

6:30.web: The apostles gathered themselves together to Jesus, and they told him all things, whatever they had done, and whatever they had taught.
6:30.kjv: And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.

bsb: they did not even have time
6:31.web: He said to them, “You come apart into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
6:31.kjv: And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

6:32.web: They went away in the boat to a deserted place by themselves.
6:32.kjv: And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.

6:33.web: They saw them going, and many recognized him and ran there on foot from all the cities. They arrived before them and came together to him.
6:33.kjv: And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.

6:34.web: Jesus came out, saw a great multitude, and he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd, and he began to teach them many things.
6:34.kjv: And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.

6:35.web: When it was late in the day, his disciples came to him, and said, “This place is deserted, and it is late in the day.
6:35.kjv: And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:

6:36.web: Send them away, that they may go into the surrounding country and villages, and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.”
6:36.kjv: Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.

6:37.web: But he answered them, “You give them something to eat.” They asked him, “Shall we go and buy two hundred denarii worth of bread, and give them something to eat?”
6:37.kjv: He answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?

6:38.web: He said to them, “How many loaves do you have? Go see.” When they knew, they said, “Five, and two fish.”
6:38.kjv: He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.

6:39.web: He commanded them that everyone should sit down in groups on the green grass.
6:39.kjv: And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.

6:40.web: They sat down in ranks, by hundreds and by fifties.
6:40.kjv: And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

6:41.web: He took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed and broke the loaves, and he gave to his disciples to set before them, and he divided the two fish among them all.
6:41.kjv: And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.

6:42.web: They all ate, and were filled.
6:42.kjv: And they did all eat, and were filled.

6:43.web: They took up twelve baskets full of broken pieces and also of the fish.
6:43.kjv: And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.

6:44.web: Those who ate the loaves were five thousand men.
6:44.kjv: And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.

6:45.web: Immediately he made his disciples get into the boat, and to go ahead to the other side, to Bethsaida, while he himself sent the multitude away.
6:45.kjv: And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.

6:46.web: After he had taken leave of them, he went up the mountain to pray.
6:46.kjv: And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.

6:47.web: When evening had come, the boat was in the middle of the sea, and he was alone on the land.
6:47.kjv: And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.

6:48.web: Seeing them distressed in rowing, for the wind was contrary to them, about the fourth watch of the night he came to them, walking on the sea, and he would have passed by them,
6:48.kjv: And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.

6:49.web: but they, when they saw him walking on the sea, supposed that it was a ghost, and cried out;
6:49.kjv: But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:

6:50.web: for they all saw him, and were troubled. But he immediately spoke with them, and said to them, “Cheer up! It is I! Don’t be afraid.”
6:50.kjv: For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.

6:51.web: He got into the boat with them; and the wind ceased, and they were very amazed among themselves, and marveled;
6:51.kjv: And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.

6:52.web: for they hadn’t understood about the loaves, but their hearts were hardened.
6:52.kjv: For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.

6:53.web: When they had crossed over, they came to land at Gennesaret, and moored to the shore.
6:53.kjv: And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.

6:54.web: When they had come out of the boat, immediately the people recognized him,
6:54.kjv: And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,

6:55.web: and ran around that whole region, and began to bring those who were sick, on their mats, to where they heard he was.
6:55.kjv: And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

6:56.web: Wherever he entered, into villages, or into cities, or into the country, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might just touch the fringe of his garment; and as many as touched him were made well.
6:56.kjv: And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.

7:1.web: Then the Pharisees and some of the scribes gathered together to him, having come from Jerusalem.
7:1.kjv: Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.

7:2.web: Now when they saw some of his disciples eating bread with defiled, that is unwashed, hands, they found fault.
7:2.kjv: And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.

7:3.web: (For the Pharisees and all the Jews, don’t eat unless they wash their hands and forearms, holding to the tradition of the elders.
7:3.kjv: For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.

7:4.web: They don’t eat when they come from the marketplace unless they bathe themselves, and there are many other things, which they have received to hold to: washings of cups, pitchers, bronze vessels, and couches.)
7:4.kjv: And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.

7:5.web: The Pharisees and the scribes asked him, “Why don’t your disciples walk according to the tradition of the elders, but eat their bread with unwashed hands?”
7:5.kjv: Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

7:6.web: He answered them, “Well did Isaiah prophesy of you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
7:6.kjv: He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.

7:7.web: But they worship me in vain, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men.’
7:7.kjv: Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.

7:8.web: “For you set aside the commandment of God, and hold tightly to the tradition of men—the washing of pitchers and cups, and you do many other such things.”
7:8.kjv: For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.

7:9.web: He said to them, “Full well do you reject the commandment of God, that you may keep your tradition.
7:9.kjv: And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.

7:10.web: For Moses said, ‘Honor your father and your mother;’ and, ‘He who speaks evil of father or mother, let him be put to death.’
7:10.kjv: For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:

7:11.web: But you say, ‘If a man tells his father or his mother, “Whatever profit you might have received from me is Corban, that is to say, given to God”;’
7:11.kjv: But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.

7:12.web: then you no longer allow him to do anything for his father or his mother,
7:12.kjv: And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;

7:13.web: making void the word of God by your tradition, which you have handed down. You do many things like this.”
7:13.kjv: Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.

7:14.web: He called all the multitude to himself, and said to them, “Hear me, all of you, and understand.
7:14.kjv: And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:

7:15.web: There is nothing from outside of the man, that going into him can defile him; but the things which proceed out of the man are those that defile the man.
7:15.kjv: There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.

7:16.web: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear!”
7:16.kjv: If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.

7:17.web: When he had entered into a house away from the multitude, his disciples asked him about the parable.
7:17.kjv: And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.

7:18.web: He said to them, “Are you also without understanding? Don’t you perceive that whatever goes into the man from outside can’t defile him,
7:18.kjv: And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;

7:19.web: because it doesn’t go into his heart, but into his stomach, then into the latrine, thus purifying all foods?”
7:19.kjv: Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?

7:20.web: He said, “That which proceeds out of the man, that defiles the man.
7:20.kjv: And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.

7:21.web: For from within, out of the hearts of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, sexual sins, murders, thefts,
7:21.kjv: For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,

7:22.web: covetings, wickedness, deceit, lustful desires, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, and foolishness.
7:22.kjv: Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:

7:23.web: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.”
7:23.kjv: All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.

7:24.web: From there he arose, and went away into the borders of Tyre and Sidon. He entered into a house, and didn’t want anyone to know it, but he couldn’t escape notice.
7:24.kjv: And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.

7:25.web: For a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell down at his feet.
7:25.kjv: For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:

7:26.web: Now the woman was a Greek, a Syrophoenician by race. She begged him that he would cast the demon out of her daughter.
7:26.kjv: The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.

7:27.web: But Jesus said to her, “Let the children be filled first, for it is not appropriate to take the children’s bread and throw it to the dogs.”
7:27.kjv: But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.

7:28.web: But she answered him, “Yes, Lord. Yet even the dogs under the table eat the children’s crumbs.”
7:28.kjv: And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.

7:29.web: He said to her, “For this saying, go your way. The demon has gone out of your daughter.”
7:29.kjv: And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.

7:30.web: She went away to her house, and found the child having been laid on the bed, with the demon gone out.
7:30.kjv: And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.

7:31.web: Again he departed from the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and came to the sea of Galilee, through the middle of the region of Decapolis.
7:31.kjv: And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.

7:32.web: They brought to him one who was deaf and had an impediment in his speech. They begged him to lay his hand on him.
7:32.kjv: And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.

7:33.web: He took him aside from the multitude, privately, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue.
7:33.kjv: And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;

7:34.web: Looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said to him, “Ephphatha!” that is, “Be opened!”
7:34.kjv: And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.

7:35.web: Immediately his ears were opened, and the impediment of his tongue was released, and he spoke clearly.
7:35.kjv: And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.

7:36.web: He commanded them that they should tell no one, but the more he commanded them, so much the more widely they proclaimed it.
7:36.kjv: And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;

7:37.web: They were astonished beyond measure, saying, “He has done all things well. He makes even the deaf hear, and the mute speak!”
7:37.kjv: And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.

8:1.web: In those days, when there was a very great multitude, and they had nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to himself, and said to them,
8:1.kjv: In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and saith unto them,

8:2.web: “I have compassion on the multitude, because they have stayed with me now three days, and have nothing to eat.
8:2.kjv: I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:

8:3.web: If I send them away fasting to their home, they will faint on the way, for some of them have come a long way.”
8:3.kjv: And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.

8:4.web: His disciples answered him, “From where could one satisfy these people with bread here in a deserted place?”
8:4.kjv: And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?

8:5.web: He asked them, “How many loaves do you have?” They said, “Seven.”
8:5.kjv: And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

8:6.web: He commanded the multitude to sit down on the ground, and he took the seven loaves. Having given thanks, he broke them, and gave them to his disciples to serve, and they served the multitude.
8:6.kjv: And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people.

8:7.web: They had a few small fish. Having blessed them, he said to serve these also.
8:7.kjv: And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.

8:8.web: They ate, and were filled. They took up seven baskets of broken pieces that were left over.
8:8.kjv: So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets.

8:9.web: Those who had eaten were about four thousand. Then he sent them away.
8:9.kjv: And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.

8:10.web: Immediately he entered into the boat with his disciples, and came into the region of Dalmanutha.
8:10.kjv: And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.

8:11.web: The Pharisees came out and began to question him, seeking from him a sign from heaven, and testing him.
8:11.kjv: And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

8:12.web: He sighed deeply in his spirit, and said, “Why does this generation seek a sign? Most certainly I tell you, no sign will be given to this generation.”
8:12.kjv: And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.

8:13.web: He left them, and again entering into the boat, departed to the other side.
8:13.kjv: And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.

8:14.web: They forgot to take bread; and they didn’t have more than one loaf in the boat with them.
8:14.kjv: Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.

8:15.web: He warned them, saying, “Take heed: beware of the yeast of the Pharisees and the yeast of Herod.”
8:15.kjv: And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.

8:16.web: They reasoned with one another, saying, “It’s because we have no bread.”
8:16.kjv: And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread.

8:17.web: Jesus, perceiving it, said to them, “Why do you reason that it’s because you have no bread? Don’t you perceive yet, neither understand? Is your heart still hardened?
8:17.kjv: And when Jesus knew it, he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?

8:18.web: Having eyes, don’t you see? Having ears, don’t you hear? Don’t you remember?
8:18.kjv: Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?

8:19.web: When I broke the five loaves among the five thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Twelve.”
8:19.kjv: When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.

8:20.web: “When the seven loaves fed the four thousand, how many baskets full of broken pieces did you take up?” They told him, “Seven.”
8:20.kjv: And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.

8:21.web: He asked them, “Don’t you understand yet?”
8:21.kjv: And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?

8:22.web: He came to Bethsaida. They brought a blind man to him, and begged him to touch him.
8:22.kjv: And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.

8:23.web: He took hold of the blind man by the hand, and brought him out of the village. When he had spat on his eyes, and laid his hands on him, he asked him if he saw anything.
8:23.kjv: And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.

8:24.web: He looked up, and said, “I see men; for I see them like trees walking.”
8:24.kjv: And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.

8:25.web: Then again he laid his hands on his eyes. He looked intently, and was restored, and saw everyone clearly.
8:25.kjv: After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.

8:26.web: He sent him away to his house, saying, “Don’t enter into the village, nor tell anyone in the village.”
8:26.kjv: And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.

8:27.web: Jesus went out, with his disciples, into the villages of Caesarea Philippi. On the way he asked his disciples, “Who do men say that I am?”
8:27.kjv: And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?

8:28.web: They told him, “John the Baptizer, and others say Elijah, but others: one of the prophets.”
8:28.kjv: And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.

8:29.web: He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ.”
8:29.kjv: And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.

8:30.web: He commanded them that they should tell no one about him.
8:30.kjv: And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

8:31.web: He began to teach them that the Son of Man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
8:31.kjv: And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.

8:32.web: He spoke to them openly. Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.
8:32.kjv: And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

bsb: you do not have in mind
8:33.web: But he, turning around, and seeing his disciples, rebuked Peter, and said, “Get behind me, Satan! For you have in mind not the things of God, but the things of men.”
8:33.kjv: But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.

8:34.web: He called the multitude to himself with his disciples, and said to them, “Whoever wants to come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
8:34.kjv: And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.

8:35.web: For whoever wants to save his life will lose it; and whoever will lose his life for my sake and the sake of the Good News will save it.
8:35.kjv: For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.

8:36.web: For what does it profit a man, to gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?
8:36.kjv: For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?

8:37.web: For what will a man give in exchange for his life?
8:37.kjv: Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

8:38.web: For whoever will be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation, the Son of Man also will be ashamed of him, when he comes in his Father’s glory, with the holy angels.”
8:38.kjv: Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

9:1.web: He said to them, “Most certainly I tell you, there are some standing here who will in no way taste death until they see God’s Kingdom come with power.”
